conversation:
Patient: I'm 53 years old, and I'm here because I've been having chest pain when I walk. It feels like pressure in my chest, and it's been going on for about three months. I haven't been able to keep up with my walking because of it.
Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the chest pain in more detail, including its location, duration, intensity, and any associated symptoms?
Patient: I'm 53 years old, and I'm a female. The chest pain is in my chest, and it feels like pressure. It mainly happens when I'm walking, and it's been going on for about three months. It doesn't go away right away, and I haven't been able to keep up with my walking because of it. I don't have any other symptoms right now, like shortness of breath or sweating.
Doctor: Could you please provide details about your past medical history, including any previous illnesses, surgeries, or allergies?
Patient: I don't have any allergies, and I don't remember having any surgeries. I do have diabetes, and I was told I might have high blood pressure, but no one has given me medication for it yet. I'm on metformin for my diabetes.
Doctor: Could you please describe if the chest pain radiates to other areas, such as your arms, jaw, or back? Also, are there any specific activities or positions that make the pain worse or better?
Patient: The chest pain doesn't radiate anywhere else, just stays in my chest. It mainly happens when I'm walking, and it's been getting in the way of me keeping up with my walks. I haven't found anything that makes it better except maybe resting, but I haven't tried anything specific.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of any previous cardiac evaluations, such as an ECG, stress test, or echocardiogram, if available? Additionally, could you share the results of any recent blood tests, such as fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, and renal function tests?
Patient: I don't have the results of any cardiac evaluations or blood tests done recently. I was told my EKG looked normal when I was in the office, but I haven't had any other tests like a stress test or echocardiogram. I do know my blood sugars have been a little higher lately because I haven't been as active, and my HbA1c was seven before, which my doctor said was okay but could be better.
Doctor: Could you please describe any changes in the pattern of your chest pain, such as whether it has become more frequent, lasts longer, or is now accompanied by other symptoms like shortness of breath, dizziness, or nausea?
Patient: The chest pain hasn't changed much in pattern, it still mainly happens when I'm walking, and it's been about three months. It doesn't last too long once I stop, but it's been getting in the way of me walking as much as I used to. I haven't had any other symptoms like shortness of breath or dizziness with it, just the pressure in my chest.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of your most recent EKG, as well as any other cardiac evaluations or blood tests you may have had, including lipid profile, troponin levels, and a stress test if available?
Patient: I don't have the results of any recent EKG or other cardiac evaluations done outside of what was mentioned in the office, which was that the EKG looked normal. I haven't had a stress test or any blood tests like lipid profile or troponin levels recently. My doctor mentioned my HbA1c was seven before, but I don't have any other test results with me.
Doctor: Could you provide more details about your family history of cardiovascular disease, including any history of heart attacks, strokes, or hypertension in first-degree relatives?
Patient: I don't know the specifics of my family history regarding heart disease, but I was told there is a history of heart disease in my family. I don't have the details on exactly who or how many relatives were affected, but it's something my doctor mentioned as a concern.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of your most recent lipid profile, troponin levels, and any other cardiac blood tests you may have had? Additionally, have you had a stress test or echocardiogram in the past?
Patient: I don't have the results of any recent lipid profile or troponin tests, and I haven't had a stress test or echocardiogram in the past. My doctor only mentioned my EKG looked normal when I was in the office.
